subject: Clarify redistributed token attribution and EU VAT impact
messages:
From: Elena Rojas <elena@greenwall.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@greenwall.ai
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected spike on August invoice — token split question

Hi Priyom,

Hope you’re well. We just received the August invoice and noticed a ~38% increase in billed tokens compared to our internal metrics. Our engineers pulled logs and it looks like a large portion of the extra tokens were attributed to an internal "search-indexing" microservice that calls your embeddings endpoint via an async queue. Historically those calls were billed under our feature flag umbrella but appear to have been attributed to a separate sub-tenant after the mid-August routing change.

Two asks: can you help explain how tokens are attributed when traffic is routed through a shared ingestion pipeline (we suspect prefix-preserving caching is involved), and whether we can get a pro-rata credit for the misattributed portion while we sort our tagging? I’ve attached a small CSV sample of affected request ids (usage-sample-202608.csv) and the invoice we received.

We’re on a tight month-end close and would like to resolve this by next Friday.

Thanks —
Elena
Elena Rojas
Head of Platform
Greenwall Analytics

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rojas <elena@greenwall.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on August invoice — token split question

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. We’re looking into this and I’ve looped in Marissa (billing ops) and Karthik (billing infra) to pull the raw attribution logs. Initial read: there was a routing policy change on 2026-08-18 that introduced a temporary fallback path for low-latency ingestion endpoints which can, in edge cases, attribute tokens to the worker pool rather than the originating customer route when a prefix cache hit occurs.

Next steps from our side:
- Karthik will run an attribution replay for the request ids you sent and check the cache key resolution and tenant tags.
- Marissa will snapshot the August invoice lines and propose a temporary credit if we confirm misattribution.
- I’ll coordinate with your engineering contact for a short joint call if required.

Can you confirm a good time for a 30-minute call on Friday morning (09:00-11:00 CEST)?

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Elena Rojas <elena@greenwall.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:02:00 +0200
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected spike on August invoice — initial credits and evidence

Forwarding preliminary findings. See attachment: invoice-draft-Greenwall-202608.pdf (redacted).

On our replay of the request ids in usage-sample-202608.csv we observed the following: in ~42% of the sample, the KV cache key resolved to the ingestion-worker identity (internal tenant id) because the cache key was stripped of the feature flag prefix during the recent router optimization. Those calls were executed by the same GPU pool but should have been billed under Greenwall’s tenant.

Proposed immediate remediation:
- Apply an interim credit equal to the misattributed token count multiplied by your August effective rate (we can apply this to September invoice or issue a standalone credit memo).
- Re-run the attribution for the entire August window (we’ll need a day) and provide a full reconciliation.
- Karthik will push a config rollback to preserve the feature-flag prefix in routing keys to avoid recurrence.

I’ve drafted a credit memo and attached it; Priyom please confirm approval to issue.

—
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Lead, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rojas <elena@greenwall.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:40:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on August invoice — technical detail on attribution replay

Elena — quick technical note from the replay: the ingestion-worker identity appears when the router stripPrefix flag is true and the cache-hash function normalizes keys across feature flags. For your sample: 1) we restored original tenant tags for the requests where the original request header contained X-Client-Tenant; 2) for the requests missing that header, we used session binding heuristics (IP + API key suffix) and recovered ~70% of those to Greenwall.

Implications for VAT: because the misattribution only affected where tokens were billed (not which legal entity incurred them), the invoice metadata (billing address, VAT id) in your originally issued invoice may show Redwood as the executing worker. We will correct the invoice metadata before issuing the credit memo so the VAT treatment remains consistent (i.e., any EU VAT charged will be reflected on the corrected lines). Please note we’ll include an errata note on VAT lines in the credit memo so your finance team has clear audit evidence.

I’ll run the full-window reconciliation tonight and push the corrected usage export to the Drive link after completion.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Billing Systems

From: Elena Rojas <elena@greenwall.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on August invoice — thanks and next steps

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround and the detailed notes. We appreciate the proposed crediting approach and the plan to correct invoice VAT lines — that addresses our main concerns. A couple of clarifying asks before we close this:

1) Please confirm whether the credit will be issued as a standalone credit memo (preferred) or netted against September. We prefer a standalone memo for audit clarity.
2) Can you add a short paragraph in the credit memo explaining the cause (router stripPrefix) and the steps taken to remediate so our auditors have context?
3) Once the corrected invoice + credit memo are available, please send both PDFs and the final reconciled usage export (CSV) to finance@greenwall.ai and cc legal@greenwall.ai.

If all that’s in place we’ll sign off and close the ticket. Looking forward to the corrected docs.

Best,
Elena
